html:
October 27, 2026

Israelis vote as Netanyahu warns of Arab turnout surge

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Israel held national elections on October 27, with turnout reaching 55.7% within nine hours, a record pace. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued an emergency appeal urging Likud supporters to the polls, pointing to what he called unprecedented turnout at Arab party polling stations and warning of a government led by Mansour Abbas and Ahmed Tibi. He also accused Ra'am operatives of attempting to steal the election and cited three arrests in an alleged voter bribery case; police confirmed the arrests but no widespread fraud has been established. Arab leaders called the tactic racist, and citizens travelled from abroad to cast ballots.

James Comey charged a third time by Trump Justice Department

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Former FBI Director James Comey faces a third criminal prosecution brought under the Trump administration, according to court records released Monday. The documents allege Comey transmitted national defense information and conspired to transmit such material in October 2016, while he was FBI director. Comey said "they're back again" and "I'm still innocent," and his attorneys have filed a motion seeking dismissal.

Appeals court rules Trump's California National Guard deployment unlawful

tags: legal, politics, immigration
sources: @oafnation_actual

A federal appeals court ruled 2 to 1 that President Trump exceeded his legal authority by federalizing 4,000 California National Guard troops during the 2025 Los Angeles immigration protests. A Trump-appointed judge joined the majority. The ruling upholds an existing injunction, and further appeals remain possible.

House Judiciary Democrats release Epstein report naming Trump

tags: politics, legal
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Democrats on the House Committee on the Judiciary released a 50-page report laying out what they describe as the case against Donald Trump emerging from the Epstein files, alongside allegations that the Justice Department worked to suppress it. The report ties Trump to accusations of sexual abuse, misconduct and sex trafficking, and accuses his Justice Department of obstructing justice. Much of the underlying material in the report had already been made public.

US intelligence memo warns of advanced Iranian plots against Americans abroad

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

A newly disclosed US intelligence memo dated October 23 warns that Iranian plots to kill Americans overseas have reached advanced stages. The warning comes as US embassies across the Middle East reduce staffing and American military officials assess threats to personnel. The memo does not identify intended victims or indicate when attacks could occur.

Russian strike on Kyiv bridge prompts river crossing plan

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia struck Kyiv's South Bridge overnight, further disrupting travel for hundreds of thousands of residents after a series of attacks on bridges around the capital. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Tuesday that Kyiv will allocate 1 billion hryvnias, about $22 million, for water crossings over the Dnipro. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the strike a serious escalation.

Trump offers $1 million payments for voter fraud convictions

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

President Trump announced on Truth Social that anyone reporting voter fraud in past elections or in the upcoming 2026 midterms will be paid $1 million upon the arrest and conviction of those responsible. The payments would come from public funds. The announcement lands roughly a week before the November 3 midterm elections, and critics said it would invite mass unfounded accusations and conflicts with multiple laws.

Report says tax law shifted trillions to the wealthiest as millions lost coverage

tags: economy, health, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

An analysis citing CBO, Americans for Tax Fairness and KFF figures says America's billionaires gained roughly two trillion dollars in wealth over the past year following the tax law signed in July, with Elon Musk alone gaining more than $800 billion. Twelve million Americans, including 2.5 million children, have lost health insurance since the start of the administration, and tariffs are estimated to cost the average family about $1,745 a year. One Utah self-employed photographer's monthly premium rose from $495 to $2,168 after enhanced subsidies expired in January; 63,000 Utahns have dropped coverage since then. Medicaid cuts are scheduled to take effect after the election, with further reductions in 2027 and 2028.

Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 workers while raising AI spending

tags: tech, markets
sources: @groundnews

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees, about 27% of its global workforce, covering eligible workers at vice president level or below in the US, Canada, India and the UK. The company plans to spend $175 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, including data centers, and has excluded data center, sales and marketing staff from the buyout program. Microsoft employed 223,000 people at the end of June, down from 228,000 in December, and offered a separate early retirement program in April.

EPA plans to roll back methane rules ahead of midterms

tags: climate, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Trump administration plans to ease methane regulations, loosening Biden-era leak inspection requirements and flaring limits, with additional relief for small wells, according to a White House official. The plan is framed as a way to boost domestic energy output and reduce fuel costs. The announcement comes a week before the midterm elections and is tied to a push in Texas.

Trump Jr. hunted in Mongolia with Putin-linked Russian oligarch

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Donald Trump Jr. travelled to Mongolia in August on a hunting trip with a Russian oligarch who has criminal convictions and close ties to Vladimir Putin, according to the Financial Times. The report says the two avoided being photographed together, and that the oligarch had earlier helped finance parts of Trump Jr.'s wedding. Intelligence officials say the relationship is open to manipulation and a potential avenue of access to the president's family.

Brazil seizes Flavio Bolsonaro's passports after election defeat

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Brazilian authorities cancelled Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's passports on Tuesday after he failed to surrender them under a Supreme Court order tied to a money laundering investigation. Police are searching for Bolsonaro, whose whereabouts are unknown following his loss to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday; he denies wrongdoing and has called for the results to be annulled, though his Liberal Party has acknowledged Lula's victory. Argentine authorities reported no record of his entering the country and denied receiving an asylum request, while Brazilian police said he had not crossed an official border checkpoint. Reporting indicates he fears imprisonment and that his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, jailed over an attempted coup, may die in prison.

Trump and Talarico hold dueling Texas rallies in tight Senate race

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump campaigned in Corpus Christi and Lubbock on Tuesday for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, while Democrat James Talarico held his own Lubbock rally the same evening. Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, and recent polling puts the Texas race in a dead heat. Texas has not elected a Democrat statewide since 1994.

Federal judge blocks construction of Trump's Washington golf course

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction halting further construction of a golf course at East Potomac Park in Washington, DC, barring the removal of additional trees. The case was brought by Democracy Forward, and the judge pointed to the president's own public statements about the project in rejecting the Justice Department's arguments. Trump responded with a lengthy post on Truth Social criticising the ruling.

Court orders Abbott to release Musk communications to rival candidate

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Travis County Judge Catherine Moussey ruled that Texas Governor Greg Abbott must allow gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa to review more than 1,000 pages of unredacted communications between Abbott and Elon Musk, according to the Hinojosa campaign. Abbott had sought to withhold the records, describing them as intimate and embarrassing. The communications are said to cover Musk's political contributions in Texas, economic development incentives and benefits received by his companies.

Book alleges Dutch spies monitored Kushner's phone and tracked Gulf payments

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @ericmoutsos

A book excerpt reports that Dutch intelligence learned Russian operatives had hacked Jared Kushner's phone in 2017 and subsequently gained access themselves, capturing images of his screen as he used it. The account claims Dutch agents observed him logging into a United Arab Emirates account that had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan, and alleges Saudi and Emirati leaders placed at least $2 billion into accounts linked to Kushner, including one with Israel's central bank. The funds were said to be disguised as government or charitable money but intended for off-the-books diplomatic objectives, including efforts to broker an Israeli-Palestinian deal, with roughly $1 billion described as allocated for Kushner's personal benefit.

Program says it has taken US judges on sponsored trips to Israel

tags: legal, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

An organiser said his program has taken federal judges to Israel on repeated trips since the start of the war, claiming roughly 10% of all active federal judges in America have participated over the past three years. He said he has now completed the first such trip for state Supreme Court justices, after receiving interest from state judges, including members of the Texas Supreme Court. The claims were not independently substantiated.

North Korean artillery and troops reported moving to the border

tags: defence, war
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Newly circulated footage shows North Korean artillery and soldiers being stationed near the border with South Korea. Sources described the movement as outside normal routine rather than a regular occurrence. No escalation has been confirmed.

Governments issue preparedness warnings as US hardens base power supplies

tags: defence, tech
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Several governments have urged citizens to prepare for disruption, with the United Kingdom advising people to be ready for three days and citing extreme weather or cyber warfare, and Japan, Sweden and Norway issuing their own warnings. The United States is implementing a program called Fortress to make continental military bases self-sufficient and independent of the civilian power grid. US officials attribute the effort to the potential for cyber warfare, echoing the British rationale.

Utah city's Meta data center tax breaks draw scrutiny as property taxes rise

tags: tech, economy
sources: @carolinegleich

In 2018, Eagle Mountain's taxing entities waived 100% of Meta's personal property tax and 80% of its real property tax for 40 years for an AI data center. If Meta builds every phase of the project, those breaks could reach $750 million. This year Eagle Mountain raised its city property tax by about 70%, roughly $99 more annually on a median home.

Energy Department appeals hundreds of Hanford workers' compensation claims

tags: health, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Department of Energy has filed more than 500 appeals over compensation claims involving sick nuclear workers at Washington's Hanford site. An investigation found about 152 state-approved claims remain under appeal, roughly half of them involving workers who have died. The department has spent nearly $12 million on outside attorneys and expert testimony since 2018.

Massachusetts gun registration takes effect days before repeal vote

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Massachusetts' firearm registration requirements become mandatory on October 28, six days before voters decide whether to keep or repeal the state's 2024 gun law. Firearms already registered do not need to be registered again. Question 9 on the November 3 ballot will determine whether the law remains in place.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern propose $85 billion rail merger

tags: markets, climate
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern have proposed an $85 billion merger that would create the first coast-to-coast single-line freight railroad in the United States. The companies say the combination would save shippers $3.5 billion annually. Estimates also indicate it could cut carbon emissions by up to 3.8 million metric tons a year.

Catholic bishops apologise for White House prayer photo op

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Catholic bishops have issued a public apology over their appearance in a photograph praying over President Trump at the White House. According to America magazine, the White House publicised and politicised the moment without the participants' consent, weeks before the midterm elections. The bishops said they regret taking part.

Obama mocks White House renovations as Trump hits back

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Campaigning in Michigan and Ohio for Democratic candidates including Senate contender Abdul El-Sayed, former President Barack Obama ridiculed the $900 million White House renovations, saying Trump "should be on HGTV" and that he has the building "looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory." Obama also criticised Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's focus on military fitness standards. Trump responded on Truth Social and repeatedly at a Mississippi rally, calling Obama a lousy president and defending the ballroom project while citing his withdrawal from the Iran nuclear agreement. At the Mississippi event a protester shouted at Trump about the ballroom before being removed.

Michigan voter dismisses ideology concerns over Senate nominee

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

A Michigan voter asked whether Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is too far to the left for the state said the label did not matter to her. "At this point, what do we have to worry about," she said, adding that her priority was lowering her cost of living. The exchange circulated widely a week before the midterm elections.

El Paso NAACP calls for response after KKK costume video

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The president of the El Paso NAACP, Carl B. Dwyer Jr., has urged community members and leaders to speak out after a video circulated showing individuals in Ku Klux Klan garb in the city, according to K-Fox 14. Dwyer said the organisation has heard from parents whose children came home from school upset after being called racial slurs. He said the outfits should not be dismissed as a joke or a party costume.

Manhunt underway after convicted murderer escapes Tennessee prison

tags: policing
sources: @aaronparnas

Tennessee officials confirmed that Jacob Morley, serving a life sentence for murder, has escaped from a state correctional facility. Surveillance footage shows him stealing a truck around 1am and passing the Horn Beak Fire Department, about 15 miles north of the facility. The Tennessee Department of Corrections describes him as dangerous and has told the public not to approach him.

Air Force base housing described as infested with rats and mold

tags: defence, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Deborah Oliver, the wife of an Air Force colonel, says she used MREs and bottled water to block rats from entering her family's housing at Randolph Air Force Base in Texas, and describes persistent mold and moisture problems. Years after moving out, she says she continues to battle serious illnesses and an unresolved legal case. The Air Force says it has strengthened housing oversight.

Veteran who claimed he could not walk pleads guilty to benefits fraud

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Army veteran Gregory Heimann Jr., who told the VA he had been unable to walk since 2004, pleaded guilty on October 23 after investigators repeatedly filmed him walking without assistance. Court records show he received about $244,000 in VA benefits since 2016. Authorities say he also staged an apparent drowning and fled before being arrested in 2025, and he faces up to five years in prison.

Report suggests Nicki Minaj press secretary talk is not a joke

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Commentator Jake LaHood says people inside Trump's orbit told him the prospect of Nicki Minaj becoming White House press secretary is a genuine possibility rather than a joke, though the timeline is unclear. The sourcing describes it as a live possibility rather than a decision. No appointment has been announced.
